Firefighters rescue multiple survivors after Brooklyn building collapse kills at least 2 people
|                            Getting your Trinity Audio player ready...                        | 
Firefighters dug through the rubble of a three-story building in Brooklyn after it collapsed at the edge of a construction site Wednesday afternoon, killing at least two people and trapping others beneath the wreckage.
News helicopter footage showed scores of firefighters scouring the debris in the borough’s Flatbush section, clambering over the rubble pile and using their hands and power saws to get through the ruins.
At least 10 people were rushed to a hospital with injuries, including four in critical condition, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said during a news conference. Fire officials said their search and rescue operations would continue for several days.
“We do not know how many people were missing overall,” said New York City Fire’s chief of department, John Esposito.
At around 6:30 p.m., firefighters pulled a dust-covered person — still alive and moving — out of a hole they had dug into the rubble pile, hoisting them up on a stretcher and rushing them to a waiting ambulance.
The building that collapsed — a mixed-use structure with apartments sitting atop businesses — had been perched at the edge of a lot where another one-story building had been torn down for a construction project. The site was being excavated, and the building that fell down filled the construction pit with bricks and wood.
Another building that shared a wall with the collapsed structure remained standing, but its wall was shorn off, exposing the rooms inside, including a bedroom and closets filled with clothing.
A drone hovered over the site as firefighters dug by hand, tossing chunks of rubble aside. Rescuers also used dogs to sniff for survivors. As darkness fell, firefighters used flashlights to illuminate the area where they worked.
“As emergency operations continue, please join me in holding our neighbors and the members of this community in our hearts,” Mamdani said in a statement posted to social media.
Phone and email messages seeking comment were left with the architect, property owner and general contractor listed in city records as being associated with the construction project.
One resident of the collapsed building, Anderson Velez, told the New York Post he was at work when his wife called and said she and their two kids, ages 7 and 2, were trapped in the wreckage.
“She called me when the building collapsed while she was inside with rubble on top of her. She was screaming for someone to help get my son out and then the call cut off,” he said.
Velez later learned that his family had been pulled from the rubble alive, he added.

At least one dead, 10 injured in Brooklyn building collapse
sources.text:
At least one person was killed and 10 others were injured when a three-story building collapsed in Brooklyn, New York, on Wednesday afternoon, CNN reported, citing a fire department official.
Four of the injured were in serious condition, while at least one person remained trapped beneath the rubble as emergency crews continued searching the site.
The collapse occurred at approximately 4:00 p.m. local time in Flatbush, a largely residential neighborhood in central Brooklyn with a predominantly Black and Afro-Caribbean population.
New York City Council member Farah N. Louis told Spectrum News NY1 that a child was among those injured.
According to a fire department official, the building contained a ground-floor store and at least one residential apartment on an upper floor. A construction site was located immediately adjacent to the collapsed structure.
The New York City Department of Buildings dispatched investigators to the scene to determine what caused the collapse.
New York State Assembly member Rodneyse Bichotte Hermelyn told NY1 that the neighboring property had remained vacant for an extended period and had previously housed a senior adult day care facility.
“That particular lot has been vacant for a long time. It used to be a senior, adult day care," she said. “They were waiting for a permit to build affordable housing. We don’t know the details in terms of why the building collapsed but all I know is it’s been probably neglected."
Emergency personnel launched an extensive search-and-rescue operation, with dozens of firefighters working through the wreckage as daylight faded.
Footage from the scene showed firefighters extracting a victim from a large pile of debris before four responders carried the person away on a stretcher.
Rescue teams also deployed drones to assist their search and used flashlights as darkness approached.
Video captured firefighters moving household items, including pillows and a damaged oven, while digging through the collapsed structure in an effort to locate additional victims.
A large crowd assembled behind police tape along the sidewalk, with bystanders recording the rescue operation as emergency vehicles lined the street.
New York City Emergency Management established a Red Cross assistance center to provide support to Flatbush residents affected by the collapse.

sources.news_title: 1 Dead, 10 Injured After Brooklyn Building Collapses into Construction Site
sources.text:
The New York City Fire Department said Wednesday that one person was killed and at least ten others were injured when a three-story Brooklyn building collapsed into an adjoining construction site.
Firefighters got the first 911 call at 4:01 p.m. and worked in debris in a construction pit in the borough’s Flatbush neighborhood, ABC News reported. Fire officials were still trying to account for every worker on the job site.
The city’s Department of Buildings (DOB) said its inspectors were dispatched to examine the surrounding block. Inspectors are “assisting with recovery operations and conducting structural stability inspections of nearby buildings,” the agency said.
Firefighters pronounced one person dead at the scene. One victim was carried out with CPR in progress, and crews were still working to reach two more people at press time, amNewYork reported. Four of the injured were in critical condition, according to the fire department.
City inspectors had flagged problems at the project next door months earlier. In May, the buildings department recorded that work had continued while a stop work order was in effect, that neighboring properties lacked proper overhead protection, and that the work did not conform to approved construction drawings, Spectrum News NY1 reported. City records identify the collapsed structure as a three-story, mixed-use building on Flatbush Avenue with four residential units.
The same site drew a violation in April after inspectors said an entire building there had been torn down despite a city order halting all demolition work, CBS New York reported. PIX11, citing city records, identified the citation as a Class 1 violation and reported that N Tech Design of America, the demolition firm working at the neighboring site, allegedly demolished a one-story building while the order was active.
It was not immediately clear whether the collapse was connected to the demolition next door, and the buildings department is investigating.
A Bronx apartment complex Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) visited in January, when he introduced his housing commissioner, carried 194 open housing-code violations, 88 of them rated immediately hazardous.
In July, two columns buckled inside a 37-story, office-to-residential conversion in Midtown Manhattan, the former Pfizer headquarters, and seven surrounding buildings were evacuated, including offices, hotels, and schools. Public records showed a history of safety violations and fines at the property, Fox 5 NY reported.
The mayor signed the Community Opportunity to Purchase Act on Tuesday, a measure affecting roughly 2,100 properties. He claimed in August that none of the 180 inspections carried out after the Midtown incident turned up an immediate threat to the public, though some ended in stop-work orders.
“The safety of New Yorkers is paramount,” Mamdani said at the time.

Pregnant woman rescued from Brooklyn building rubble as husband interviewed live on TV
In a building collapse in Brooklyn where one person has died and others have been critically injured, rescuers pulled a pregnant woman from the rubble
Rescuers pulled a pregnant woman alive from the rubble of a collapsed Brooklyn building Wednesday evening, moments after her husband was shown on live TV frantically trying to get past police to reach her before he knew her fate.
Her husband was one of many onlookers surrounding the building as he waited for news of his loved one after a tragic building collapse at 2625 Bedford Avenue. One person was killed and more than a dozen injured, with reports at 6 p.m. suggesting at least four were in critical condition.
Public Advocate Jumaane Williams joined the husband and other family members at the scene, and was seen standing with the man after he was interviewed about his pregnant wife on TV. A CBS journalist was able to provide him with photos of the dramatic rescue of the woman captured by helicopter footage. She was pulled from the rubble shortly after 6:30 p.m.

Her husband burst into tears after he realized his pregnant wife was alive and was receiving medical attention. Williams embraced the man after learning the news. He later confirmed that she and the baby are okay, and said that she is six months pregnant.
He told cameras, "My wife! She is alive. She is still alive. I am very happy, I am very happy. I thank everyone."
Moments before, the woman’s husband had been on scene in Flatbush in visible distress, telling reporters he had been unable to reach his wife and feared she was trapped inside. “No, I have nothing. I call, I call her. Nobody answering,” he said when asked if he’d heard from her. When pressed on whether she was in the building, he replied, “Yes, she's inside the building. She's pregnant.”
He was then seen breaking away from reporters to run to police at a barricade, visibly anxious as he tried to get police to let him through the barricade as officers tried to direct him.
The building suffered a complete collapse shortly after 4 p.m. Wednesday, prompting a large-scale FDNY response. Footage from the scene showed walls and roofing pancaked and fractured, exposing interior spaces as emergency crews carried out what officials described as a “frantic but careful” search for anyone buried beneath debris.

After 7 p.m., officers brought in dogs, hoping they could sniff out more people who required rescuing. The effort is expected to go on through the night, with cranes and other equipment now being brought in to carefully remove the rubble.
Witnesses described a sudden, terrifying scene as the structure gave way. “It sounded like a massive explosion or a heavy truck crashing, and within seconds the entire street was choked with a thick cloud of dust,” Marcus Vance told La Voce di New York.
The cause of the collapse remains under investigation. Early reports and video from the scene suggested construction activity was underway, leaving upper floors and internal framework exposed, according to the outlet.
Authorities urged the public to avoid the area. “We are asking everyone to stay well clear of the area to ensure unobstructed access for heavy rescue equipment and emergency vehicles,” police said in an early briefing.
City records show the Department of Buildings issued a violation to a demolition contractor in April after inspectors found an entire structure on the site had been torn down earlier this year despite a stop-work order.
The violation is now marked resolved, though the notice does not specify why the stop-work order was originally issued. Records also show construction activity continued at the location after the demolition, though it is not yet clear whether that work is related to Wednesday’s collapse.
Elected officials reacted with shock as rescue crews continued working into the evening. NYC Council Member Farah Louis, who represents Flatbush, said, “We are devastated to learn that at least one life has been lost, with multiple people reported trapped and several injured as emergency personnel work urgently to reach everyone in the rubble.
“My immediate priority is the safety of everyone impacted, and my team is actively working to reach affected families to connect them with critical information and support during this frightening time.”
Congresswoman Yvette Clarke said she was “heartbroken” and added: “My thoughts and prayers are with everyone affected, particularly those trapped beneath the rubble and their loved ones as they endure this difficult and uncertain time.”
She added, “My office stands ready to assist affected residents and their families as the situation unfolds. I urge everyone to avoid the area and allow emergency personnel the space and resources needed to carry out their critical response and rescue operations.”

NEW YORK, Nov 11 (Reuters) – The collapse of a three-story apartment building in Brooklyn killed at least one person and injured at least 10 others on Wednesday, the New York City Fire Department said.
Dozens of firefighters and a search dog could be seen combing through the rubble, removing debris by the bucketful, at the four-unit building built in 1930. Drone footage from local television station WABC showed a stove, a toilet and a door amid debris that had fallen into a pit at an adjacent construction site. Construction workers were among the injured, according to local media reports.
Two and a half hours after the collapse, a person was pulled alive from the rubble, put on a stretcher and taken away in an ambulance, WABC footage showed.
“I’m very happy, I’m very happy,” a man who believed the person was his six-month-pregnant wife told a WABC reporter.
Later, as flashlight beams bounced off strips of reflective tape on rescuers’ dark coats, another person could be seen being pulled alive from the rubble.
The Fire Department said it received a call about the full collapse of a building just after 4 p.m. Eastern time (2100 GMT) on Wednesday.
The Fire Department had said four people were critically injured and six more sustained minor injuries before two people were rescued.

Firefighters were called to the scene in Flatbush around 4 p.m. and rescued a person alive from the debris at about 6:30 p.m. At least four people were hospitalized in critical condition, and six others were treated for minor injuries.
Key Facts
- The New York City Fire Department said one person had died and at least four people were taken to a hospital in critical condition.
- The construction site was being excavated after a one-story building on the lot had been torn down.
- A neighboring building remained standing, but the collapse sheared off its shared wall and exposed rooms inside.
- Rescuers searched by hand and used dogs to look for survivors as darkness fell.
- Mayor Zohran Mamdani asked people to keep the community and emergency responders in their thoughts in a social media statement.
NEW YORK — Firefighters dug through the rubble of a three-story building in Brooklyn on Wednesday after it collapsed at the edge of a construction site, killing at least two people and trapping others beneath the wreckage.
Firefighters were called to the scene in the borough's Flatbush section around 4 p.m. News helicopter footage showed dozens of firefighters scouring the debris, clambering over the rubble pile and using their hands and power saws to cut through the ruins.
One person died, and at least four others were rushed to a hospital in critical condition, according to the New York City Fire Department. Six additional people were taken to hospitals with minor injuries.
At around 6:30 p.m., firefighters pulled a dust-covered person — still alive and moving — out of a hole they had dug into the rubble pile, hoisting them up on a stretcher and rushing them to a waiting ambulance.
The building that collapsed had been perched at the edge of a lot where another one-story building had been torn down for a construction project. The site was being excavated, and the building that fell down filled the construction pit with bricks and wood.
Another building that shared a wall with the collapsed structure remained standing, but its wall was shorn off, exposing the rooms inside, including a bedroom and closets filled with clothing.
A drone hovered over the site as firefighters dug by hand, tossing chunks of rubble aside. Rescuers also used dogs to sniff for survivors. As darkness fell, firefighters used flashlights to illuminate the area where they worked.
“As emergency operations continue, please join me in holding our neighbors and the members of this community in our hearts,” Mayor Zohran Mamdani said in a statement posted on social media.
Phone and email messages seeking comment were left with the architect, property owner and general contractor listed in city records as being associated with the construction project.

sources.text:
Two people are dead, and at least 19 others were injured after a building collapsed in Brooklyn on Wednesday afternoon.
Firefighters responded to a complete building collapse near the corner of Flatbush and Bedford Avenues in Flatbush shortly after 4 p.m. on Nov. 11, where several construction workers were trapped beneath the debris.
EMS units pronounced one person dead at the scene; Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Thursday evening that a second person had died from their injuries. Officials said two others were in critical condition, and a search for others trapped remains ongoing.
“The Department of Buildings and our law enforcement partners will be leading an investigation into what caused this building to collapse,” Mamdani told reporters at a Wednesday evening press conference steps away from the ongoing rescue operation. “This was a devastating collapse, and we know that it affects the lives of many New Yorkers who were directly impacted.”
Seven of the 19 injured people are children of unknown ages, Fire Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore said. Four of the 19 victims were still hospitalized in critical condition as of 8 p.m. Wednesday night; another 12 were listed in stable condition. One firefighter has been treated for minor injuries.
FDNY sources said the incident saw the rear portion of 1325 Flatbush Ave., a three-story building, completely collapsed into a neighboring open construction site on Bedford Avenue. FDNY, NYPD and paramedics rushed to the scene after receiving a call about the collapse at 4:01 p.m.
Fire department personnel removed multiple construction workers from the rubble and were working to rescue additional people at press time, officials said.
“Flatbush Avenue is closed from Clarendon Road to Bedford Avenue – please avoid the area so rescue crews can work. We will be sharing what we learn as soon as we can confirm it,” Mamdani said in a social media statement. “As emergency operations continue, please join me in holding our neighbors and the members of this community in our hearts.”
At least one person was removed from the building with CPR in progress. The condition of the workers was not immediately known.
The Department of Buildings was on site to assist with recovery efforts and conduct structural stability inspections of nearby buildings. Buildings Commissioner Ahmed Tigani indicated that construction crews at the nearby work site were conducting excavation work prior to the collapse.
More than 250 FDNY personnel responded to the site. Bonsignore said the operations are expected to last throughout the night Wednesday, as it remains unknown how many more people are trapped in the rubble.
“This will be a prolonged operation,” Bonsignore said. “We expect there could be more people found as this operation progresses. The units are performing dangerous and heroic work. … We know we are not finished here, and we will likely not be finished here for quite some time.”
Ace Rogers, an eyewitness, described a loud banging sound when the building collapsed.
“Coming from work, all I hear is two loud bangs; it scared the s–t out of me,” Rogers said. “I’ve never seen cops and firefighters in Flatbush. I’ve never seen this before.”
Firefighters and emergency personnel remained at the scene as rescue operations continued late into the afternoon. It is not yet known what caused the collapse.
Rep. Yvette Clarke, who represents the area, said she is monitoring the situation.
“I commend the FDNY, NYPD, EMS personnel, and all first responders working tirelessly on the scene to rescue those trapped and ensure the safety of our community,” she said. “My staff and I are closely monitoring the situation and will remain in contact with local officials, first responders, and Community Board 17 as more information becomes available.”
Emergency personnel are asking the public to avoid the area as rescue and response operations continue.
“We’re closely monitoring the building collapse on Bedford Avenue in Flatbush,” Public Advocate Jumaane Williams wrote on X. “We’re praying for the safety of anyone who may be trapped and for the first responders working to reach them. Our thoughts are with everyone affected and their loved ones.”
The city’s Emergency Management Department has established a reception center at the Flatbush YMCA, 1401 Flatbush Ave., for any residents directly impacted by the building collapse to receive services.

Multiple people are reportedly trapped after a three-storey building partially collapsed in the Flatbush area of Brooklyn
Multiple people are trapped inside a building in Brooklyn after it partially collapsed, according to emergency officials.
Emergency crews raced to the scene of the three-storey building in the largely residential area of Flatbush shortly after 4pm on Wednesday.
At least one person has been confirmed dead, while six others have been taken to hospital with injuries. People remain trapped beneath the rubble, prompting a complex and ongoing technical rescue operation, the fire department said.
News helicopter footage showed dozens of firefighters scouring the debris, with a group homing in on one area and appearing to use a saw to cut through the wreckage.
"FDNY units are currently operating at a building collapse on Flatbush Avenue in Brooklyn," the department said in a statement Wednesday afternoon.
"Our units arrived to a heavy structural collapse with active reports of individuals entrapped. This is a delicate and high-risk technical rescue operation," an FDNY spokesperson said at the scene.
At around 6.30pm, firefighters pulled a dust-covered person — still alive and moving — out of a hole they had dug into the rubble pile, hoisting them up on a stretcher and rushing them to a waiting ambulance.

NYC building collapse: One dead, several injured after three-storey structure partially collapses in Brooklyn
A partial building collapse in Brooklyn brought emergency crews to the scene Wednesday afternoon.
One dead and several injured after a mixed-use three-storey building partially collapsed in the Flatbush area of Brooklyn, New York, on Wednesday afternoon, November 11. The collapse happened near Bedford and Flatbush Avenues, according to PIX11.
Video shared by Citizen showed the inside of what appeared to be apartment units exposed to the outdoors, from the roof down to the first floor.
Watch the video here.
Fire Department of New York (FDNY) crews were seen at the scene around 4 p.m. working to contain the situation. Officials had not confirmed any injuries or identified what caused the collapse.
Death toll and injuries confirmed
At least one person has died and several others have been injured in the collapse, according to abc7. Firefighters are continuing their search for another person trapped in the rubble and remain in communication with them.
Several injured construction workers were taken to Kings County Hospital, though their conditions were not immediately known. Search and rescue operations remain underway.
According to reports citing FDNY radio communications, the collapse has left atleast 10 others injured.
People reportedly trapped after Brooklyn building collapse
Emergency crews are responding to a reported partial building collapse at an apartment building in Brooklyn, with people reportedly trapped inside, according to FDNY officials cited by ABC7 New York.

The incident occurred shortly after 4 pm Wednesday at 2625 Bedford Avenue, between Newkirk and Flatbush avenues.
Aerial footage from NewsCopter 7 appeared to show several rooms inside the building exposed after part of the structure gave way.
First responders were at the scene as emergency crews worked to assess the situation. Further details about the number of people trapped, possible injuries and the cause of the collapse were not immediately available.
NYPD issues traffic advisory
The New York Police Department has urged people to avoid the area around Bedford Avenue and Flatbush Avenue following the collapse.
In a post on X, the NYPD warned that street closures and traffic delays are expected and advised motorists to take alternate routes.
See the before/after photo of the collapsed building here.
Hochul and Mamdani respond
New York Governor Kathy Hochul expressed her condolences to the family of the person who died in the Brooklyn building collapse. In a post on X, she said,
“My heart breaks for the family who lost a loved one in today’s building collapse in Brooklyn. My administration has reached out and offered its full support as authorities investigate what happened.”
New York City Mayor Zohran Kwame Mamdani also addressed the incident, saying first responders were working to secure the site and help residents.
In his post on X, Mamdani said, “Flatbush Avenue is closed from Clarendon Road to Bedford Avenue – please avoid the area so rescue crews can work.”
He added that the city would share further information once officials could confirm the details.

One dead, several persons trapped after building collapses in New York

One dead, several persons trapped after building collapses in New York

NEW YORK (AP) – Firefighters dug through the rubble of a three-story building in Brooklyn on Wednesday after it collapsed at the edge of a construction site, killing at least one person and trapping others beneath the wreckage.
Firefighters were called to the scene in the borough's Flatbush section around 4:00 pm. News helicopter footage showed dozens of firefighters scouring the debris, clambering over the rubble pile and using their hands and power saws to cut through the ruins.
One person died, and at least four others were rushed to a hospital in critical condition, according to the New York City Fire Department. Six additional people were taken to hospitals with minor injuries.
At around 6:30 pm, firefighters pulled a dust-covered person – still alive and moving – out of a hole they had dug into the rubble pile, hoisting them up on a stretcher and rushing them to a waiting ambulance.
The building that collapsed had been perched at the edge of a lot where another one-story building had been torn down for a construction project. The site was being excavated, and the building that fell down filled the construction pit with bricks and wood.
Another building that shared a wall with the collapsed structure remained standing, but its wall was shorn off, exposing the rooms inside, including a bedroom and closets filled with clothing.
A drone hovered over the site as firefighters dug by hand, tossing chunks of rubble aside. Rescuers also used dogs to sniff for survivors. As darkness fell, firefighters used flashlights to illuminate the area where they worked.
"As emergency operations continue, please join me in holding our neighbors and the members of this community in our hearts," Mayor Zohran Mamdani said in a statement posted on social media.
Phone and email messages seeking comment were left with the architect, property owner and general contractor listed in city records as being associated with the construction project.

According to city records reviewed by CBS New York, a demolition contractor was cited in April after a building was taken down despite an order to halt demolition work. The violation was subsequently marked resolved, and the notice did not explain the reason for the original stop-work order.
Investigators have not said that the earlier violation, demolition work or excavation caused Wednesday’s collapse. The Department of Buildings said its commissioner and investigators were heading to the location to assess the damage. Any finding about what went wrong will depend on an examination of the site, construction records and the affected structures.
Glenn Corbett, an associate professor of fire science at John Jay College, told CBS New York that deep excavation beside an existing building can create structural risks if appropriate precautions are not taken. Such work, he explained, “can often present a lot of precarious problems of destabilizing an existing building.” He did not establish that excavation caused this particular collapse.
The Brooklyn building collapse also disrupted traffic in the immediate neighborhood. Officials warned motorists to avoid Bedford Avenue near the emergency scene because of road closures and delays. With fire crews, medical responders, and building inspectors operating in a limited space, keeping nearby streets clear was part of the immediate public safety response.
Several questions remained unresolved as rescuers worked: how many people were on the property when the structure gave way, whether everyone had been located, and what caused a three-story building to come down. No fatalities had been confirmed in the reports available at the time of writing, and no final accounting of the people affected had been released.
As firefighters continued searching, city building investigators prepared to examine the damaged structure and surrounding construction activity. Their findings will help determine what led to the collapse and whether nearby properties face additional structural risks.

sources.news_title: Multiple People Trapped in Brooklyn Building Collapse: 4 Injured, One Critically
sources.text:
On Wednesday afternoon just after 4:00 PM EST, emergency crews rushed to the scene of a dangerous building collapse in the Flatbush neighborhood of Brooklyn. The partial structural failure occurred along Bedford Avenue between Newkirk and Flatbush avenues, instantly drawing a massive emergency response.
According to the Fire Department of New York (FDNY), there are at least one dead, one in critical condition and at least 9 others injured. Others may still be trapped. The partial collapse prompted a complex and ongoing technical rescue operation. “Our units arrived to a heavy structural collapse with active reports of individuals entrapped. This is a delicate and high-risk technical rescue operation,” an FDNY spokesperson noted at the scene. First responders are actively combing through debris and securing the site to safely reach anyone trapped inside.
Witnesses in the neighborhood described a terrifying scene as the structure gave way. “It sounded like a massive explosion or a heavy truck crashing, and within seconds the entire street was choked with a thick cloud of dust,” said local resident Marcus Vance.
While the exact underlying causes of the collapse remain under active investigation, early reports and local visuals from the scene indicate that the affected site was under construction, exposing upper-level rooms and interior framing down to the lower floors.
Because this is a fast-moving, developing story, details regarding injuries, structural integrity, and the definitive trigger of the collapse continue to emerge as municipal authorities and engineering teams gather more information on-site. Officials have urged drivers, commuters, and pedestrians to completely avoid the Bedford Avenue corridor. “We are asking everyone to stay well clear of the area to ensure unobstructed access for heavy rescue equipment and emergency vehicles,” police officials urged during an initial briefing.

sources.news_title: NYC building collapse kills 1 and traps people in wreckage - Now Georgia
sources.text:
NEW YORK (AP) — Firefighters dug through the rubble of a three-story building in Brooklyn on Wednesday after it collapsed at the edge of a construction site, killing at least one person and trapping others beneath the wreckage.
Firefighters were called to the scene in the borough’s Flatbush section around 4 p.m. News helicopter footage showed dozens of firefighters scouring the debris, with a group homing in on one area and appearing to use a saw to cut through the wreckage.
One person was pronounced dead, and another was critically injured and rushed to a hospital, a spokesperson for the New York Police Department said. Additional people were also transported to hospitals, but their conditions were not immediately clear.
The aerial videos showed firefighters digging at least one person out of the rubble and removing them on a stretcher.
The building that collapsed had been perched at the edge of a lot where another one-story building had been torn down for a construction project. The site was being excavated, and the building that fell down filled the construction pit with bricks and wood.
Another building that shared a wall with the collapsed structure remained standing, but its wall was shorn off, exposing the rooms inside, including a bedroom and closets filled with clothing.
A drone hovered over the site as firefighters dug by hand, tossing chunks of rubble aside. Rescuers also used dogs to sniff for survivors. As darkness fell, firefighters used flashlights to illuminate the area where they worked.
Phone and email messages seeking comment were left with the architect, property owner and general contractor listed in city records as being associated with the construction project.
